_what: Every AI app or harness a person talks through, one row each. Code reads these rows and never names an app: adding an app is a row here. id: the row's stable name. app: the name its messages are kept under. product: the AI product a person knows it as, the name shown in sentences that list the AIs connected (several harnesses are one product: Claude Code and Claude are both Claude). names: other spellings that mean this app, matched ignoring case (the app name always matches). contains: words that name this app when they appear as whole words inside a longer client name (Codex Desktop 1.2, claude-ai, ChatGPT connector), ignoring case; the longest word found wins, so Claude Code is Claude Code, not Claude. turns.roads: how its turns reach Trillion (transcript-hook: a hook reads the app's own transcript; mcp-record: the AI calls record_messages; web-chat-site: a page of the chat is saved; export-import: a chat export is imported). turns.recorded_by_ai: whether the AI itself records its turns (false: a transcript hook owns both sides, so a manual record of the same chat is refused). takes_work: whether work is handed to this app (false: a message from it is decided by any AI at once, with no wait for the chat to answer first). replies.final_when: when an AI reply from this app counts as the AI's final answer. marked: only when the sender marks it (final_reply true), or when both final_reply and at are absent. recorded-live: marked, or final_reply absent with at within 10 minutes of now either way (a reply recorded as it was said, by an app that cannot mark its own final answer). source_return: how work handed to this app comes back (transcript: its final answer is found in the app's own transcript, by the same-named row in harness/record-every-message.json, and the app's source chats are named id:session UUID); absent: it does not come back that way. consults_trillion: how the app's AI is brought to read Trillion before it claims what he has, decided or is doing (road turn-end-hook: a hook at the end of each turn checks it; prompt-hook: a hook at each prompt; instructions-only: only the server instructions ask it), read_tools: the tools it reads with, claims_need_read: a claim about his state must follow a read in the same turn. standing_instructions: where the app keeps instructions it reads at the start of every conversation (kind file: a file under the app's folder in the person's home, or under its home_variable folder, which the standing-instructions tool keeps one marked block in; kind host-control: no file, the AI uses the named control of the app itself). default: the row any app without its own row uses.

standing_instructions.control: its own memory or custom instructions
ChatGPT's Custom instructions or Memory in its personalization settings
Claude's personal preferences or memory in its settings
Gemini's saved info or instructions for Gemini in its settings
Grok's custom instructions in its settings
Cursor's User Rules in its settings
